gen-dafont-college-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Every curve in College is as hefty as its straight stems, and its tall lowercase holds big counters. College hits hard; Mochiy Pop P One leaves generous gaps between letters.
gen-dafont-college-gf-montserrat-underli: College draws its curves as stoutly as its stems, leaving big counters in a tall lowercase. Montserrat Underline reads smoothly across many lines, its round, open bowls staying uniform.
gen-dafont-college-gf-mozilla-headline: College keeps its thin joins as sturdy as the stems, with big counters in a tall lowercase. College is the loud one; Mozilla Headline is the big-bodied friendly one.
gen-dafont-college-gf-mozilla-text: Chunky, confident curves: College makes every bowl as stout as its stems, with big counters. Mozilla Text looks bold beside it thanks to tall bodies and terminals that flare outward.
gen-dafont-college-gf-nata-sans: College builds curves that match its straight stems in strength, with big counters in a tall lowercase. College makes the statement; Nata Sans draws with technical-pen steadiness, curves left open.
gen-dafont-college-gf-nobile: College looks drawn with one constant pen width, its big counters sitting in a tall lowercase. Nobile feels lighter beside it, with open mouths and lowercase close to capital height.
gen-dafont-college-gf-nokora: Nokora lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its s never tightening up. What binds them is sturdiness: College has no pinched joints or flared ends.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic leaves an open, welcoming gap in the c, with capitals only slightly above lowercase. College brings flicker-free punch, while the body stays modern and tidy.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans fills most of the letter height with its lowercase, and its c is generously open. Give College size to show its rod-stock strokes, Noto Sans a modest one.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Reading Noto Sans Adlam feels clean and contemporary, its curve endings kept well apart and c, s and z standing full. Shared simplicity wins: College draws each glyph as if with one tip.
